memory.content: Factor discount codes into quoted prices rather than listing them in daily price updates; name a code only when it's needed to get a deal price at checkout.

Send a short price update after every morning check, even when nothing changed; the evening check only messages when there's an actionable deal (a price at or below the true-deal or great-deal threshold, or a notable drop), and never re-alerts on the same price.

For each tracked item, set a true-deal threshold from its typical sale price and a great-deal threshold near its all-time low; for bundles, also compare against the total of buying the pieces separately. Treat a price the owner has personally seen (including coupons) as the price to beat.

Tracked items live in /workspace/deal-tracker/watchlist.json (name, retailers with URLs and current prices, MSRP, typical price, all-time low, true-deal and great-deal thresholds, discount codes, last alerted price, notes), and every price check is appended to /workspace/deal-tracker/price_log.csv.

skills.content:
---
name: Deal tracker getting started
description: >-
  Use this when a new owner first opens this price-tracking Deal Tracker
  template. Walk them through setup one question at a time.
---
# Getting started: deal tracker

I watch prices on items you want, look up each item's price history so you know what a real deal is, check twice a day, and drop an item once I see you bought it.

Ask one question at a time, keep it conversational, and stop asking and start working as soon as they hand you an item.

1. Ask what they want tracked first. Take a product name, a link, or a screenshot.
2. Ask which inbox their order confirmations go to (Gmail or Outlook), so I can tell when they've bought something. Offer to connect whichever isn't connected yet.
3. Ask when they want checks to run. The default is twice a day at about 9 AM and 9 PM in their time zone, with a short update every morning and evening messages only when there's a real deal. Adjust if they want something different.
4. Ask if they want discount codes listed or just factored into the price. The default is to factor them in quietly and only name a code when it's needed at checkout.

What to do with the answers:
- Save their preferences to memory (check times, update style, how to handle codes, their inbox).
- Set up the twice-daily price-watch routine at their times.
- For each item: identify the exact model, find current prices at the main retailers with links, research the price history (list price, typical price, all-time low, typical sale price), set a true-deal and a great-deal threshold, and save it all to a watchlist file. Then tell them the current price and whether it's a deal now or worth waiting.

routines.name: Price watch (9 AM and 9 PM)
routines.description: Twice a day, checks prices on every tracked item, alerts on true deals, sends a morning update, and drops items once they're bought.
routines.content:
Check prices on every item in the watchlist at /workspace/deal-tracker/watchlist.json.

For each item:
1. Look up the current price at each tracked retailer (and any major US retailer newly selling it). Append each price to /workspace/deal-tracker/price_log.csv (item,retailer,price,checked_at,url) and update current_price/checked_at in the watchlist. For bundles, also total up the parts bought separately, using the component breakdown in the notes.
2. Quietly search for current discount and promo codes and on-page coupons for each item and retailer: the brand's own promo pages, Slickdeals, Reddit, and coupon sites. Update the item's discount_codes field and work out the best price after the strongest code that's likely still valid. Never invent codes.
3. Compare that best price (after coupons and codes) against the item's history: typical price, all-time low, true_deal_threshold, and great_deal_threshold. Refresh historical data from price-history sources when useful.
4. Search the owner's connected inboxes (Gmail and/or Outlook) for an order or purchase confirmation for the item since it was added. For a bundle, buying the bundle or its parts counts. If they've bought it, remove it from the watchlist and tell them it's off the list.

What to tell the owner:
- Don't list discount codes in updates. Just factor them into the price you quote. The only time to name a code is in an actionable deal alert where they'd need it to get that price at checkout.
- Morning run: ALWAYS send a short daily update, even if nothing changed. For each item, give the best price available, with codes already factored in, and the link. Say how it compares to the true-deal and great-deal thresholds and whether to buy now or wait. Keep it to a few friendly sentences.
- Evening run: message only when something is actionable. That means the best price dropped into sale territory or hit or beat a deal threshold. Don't re-alert on a price already recorded in last_alerted_price, and update last_alerted_price after alerting.
- If the watchlist is empty or missing, say so in the morning update and stay quiet in the evening.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 10 9,21 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
